scope: Read-only independent patch, test, runner and retained original RED review. No builds, native processes, benchmarks, patch applications or Git mutations by reviewer.

checks.detail: For both actual source copies, selecting the OFF preprocessor branch gives exactly the original bitboard.cpp token sequence. Selecting ON removes the old early bool and encloses the complete byte-identical old initialization body in one call_once. No table algorithm, value, search, NNUE or move-ordering change.

Only CMakeLists.txt, IDEA_SOURCE.md and src/bitboard.cpp differ among existing files in each source copy; the standalone dated test is added. L/B Board and bitboard code hashes agree, and the adopted buffer repair outside these files is retained.

One option defaults OFF. The guarded Linux GNU/Clang test target compiles the actual board.cpp and bitboard.cpp directly, links Threads, has its own TSan compile/link flags and does not link forge_core. Target-specific ASan/UBSan flags on forge_core therefore do not contaminate this TSan target. Actual registration/profile execution remains pending.

Eight threads pass one barrier before any first Board construction; main creates no Board and invokes no attacks initialization. Each worker checks start FEN, perft3=8902, restored FEN and kiwi perft2=2039. Results are distinct per worker and read after join.

Each iteration creates a separate exec via Popen, communicates to complete EOF, waits for the exit, retains exact base64 stdout/stderr and SHA256, and stops on the first nonzero exit, non-exact PASS line or any stderr. No retry, warm bootstrap, kill, pin, limit adjustment or sanitizer suppression.

Original retained run exits 66 with an actual ThreadSanitizer race on attacks::init early bool read/write through concurrent first Board constructors. Diagnostic also includes DEADLYSIGNAL; this is retained, not suppressed. It is not a TSan unexpected-memory-mapping startup failure. Test hash matches the candidate test; original source hashes match the provided base.
